This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by the Hong Kong Observatory in degrees Celsius on 29 May '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from the Hong Kong Observatory, specifically the "Absolute Daily Max (deg. C)" the specified date once information is finalized in the relevant "Daily Extract", available here: https://www.weather.gov.hk/en/cis/climat.htm

This market can not resolve until data for this date has been published.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures in Celsius to one decimal place (eg, 9.1°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is initially published for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest ensemble forecasts from global and regional models indicate a maximum temperature near 28°C in Shanghai on May 29, with variable afternoon cloud cover and light winds from the East China Sea expected to moderate peak heating. Recent model runs show slight cooling relative to the prior day’s 30°C readings, driven by increased moisture and scattered showers that reduce solar insolation. Historical May climatology places average highs near 26–27°C, while current conditions reflect typical pre-monsoon variability where small shifts in timing of cloud development or sea-breeze onset can alter the daily peak by 1–2°C. Traders thus assign comparable weight to 26–28°C outcomes, reflecting genuine forecast uncertainty that will narrow with updated high-resolution runs closer to the date.
